chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The cutting is from the middle of the palm, and the thumb is not cut; and when the foot is cut, the heel is left and is not cut.
ai.seo_question: What are the specific anatomical details for cutting the hand and foot in Islamic criminal law?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the precise anatomical boundaries for the hadd of qat' (cutting) in theft, specifying that the incision begins at the wrist joint (middle of the palm) while preserving the thumb (al-ibham) to maintain hand functionality. It further details the corresponding penalty for the foot, where the heel (al-'aqib) is left intact, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on proportionality and minimizing permanent disability beyond the prescribed punishment.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The cutting (of the hand) is from the middle of the palm, and the thumb is not cut; and when the foot is cut, the heel is not cut’.
